passages.text: The company depends on two specialist suppliers for server components. A disruption lasting more than thirty days could delay cloud infrastructure deliveries and increase operating costs.

Research and development expense increased as the company hired engineers for its new security platform. The annual report identifies higher payroll and cloud hosting costs as drivers of operating expense.
Harbor Foods recorded revenue of 4.2 billion dollars for fiscal year 2024, compared with 3.8 billion dollars in fiscal year 2023.
Operating cash flow was 920 million dollars in fiscal year 2024. The cash flow statement attributes the increase partly to collections of trade receivables.
A cybersecurity incident could expose customer information. The company uses access controls, encryption, incident exercises, and external security assessments to reduce this risk.
The company leases its office and data center properties. Future minimum operating lease payments total 610 million dollars, with the largest payments due within five years.
Remaining performance obligations were 7.4 billion dollars at year end. This contracted backlog is expected to be recognized as revenue over the next three fiscal years.
Foreign currency movements affected reported results. A stronger US dollar reduced translated international revenue by 180 million dollars during the year.
A former distributor filed a commercial lawsuit alleging breach of contract. The company disputes the allegations and states that the outcome cannot currently be estimated.
The company reports three operating segments: North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Segment revenue is reviewed by the chief operating decision maker each quarter.
